extracted.intended_audience: short-story editors, literary critics, and writers interested in magazine/short-story quality assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and metrics used in a literary yearbook to evaluate short stories and to rank magazines (asterisk distinction scale, 'distinctive' story counts/percentages, Roll of Honor selection and inclusion thresholds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction scale
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, and three asterisks are employed to indicate relative distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The yearbook uses a one-/two-/three-asterisk system to mark relative distinction among stories; the asterisks are a graded indicator of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-asterisk (highest) rating meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Three-asterisk stories" are of somewhat permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A three-asterisk designation signals the highest level of distinction in this system — stories judged to have lasting or 'somewhat permanent' literary importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive stories (count metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: No. of stories published / No. of distinctive stories published / Percentage of distinctive stories published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magazines are evaluated by raw counts of 'distinctive' stories they publish and by the percentage those distinctive stories comprise of their total fiction output; these three numbers form the core magazine-average table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking by percentage of distinctive stories
rubrics_metrics.description: BY PERCENTAGE OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES (rank list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magazines are ranked according to the percentage of their published stories judged 'distinctive'; the yearbook presents a top list by percentage (e.g., Scribner's Magazine 71%, Century 60%, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking by number of distinctive stories
rubrics_metrics.description: BY NUMBER OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES (rank list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magazines are alternatively ranked by the raw number of distinctive stories published during the year (e.g., Harper's Magazine 56, Illustrated Sunday Magazine 46, Collier's 46, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion thresholds for ranked lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The following tables indicate the rank, during 1913, by number and percentage of distinctive stories, of the eighteen periodicals coming within the scope of my examination which have published during the past year over twenty-five stories and which have exceeded an average of 13% in stories of distinction. The lists exclude reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only periodicals that meet both thresholds (more than 25 stories published in the year AND an average above 13% in stories of distinction) are included in the ranked lists; reprints are excluded from counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counts of two-asterisk and three-asterisk stories as quality indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The following periodicals have published during 1915 ten or more 'two-asterisk stories.' / The following periodicals have published during 1915 three or more 'three-asterisk' stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The yearbook tracks and reports how many higher-tier starred stories each magazine published (threshold lists for >=10 two-asterisk stories and >=3 three-asterisk stories) as an additional measure of a magazine's literary output and distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roll of Honor selection pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. — 'The Roll of Honor for 1914' is based on the reading of the eight periodicals listed on page 288.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Roll of Honor is compiled from a defined reading pool: only stories appearing in the specified eight periodicals (listed elsewhere) were considered for that year's Roll, i.e., selection is limited to a stated corpus.
